added_provisions.reason: 15-1876/s21(1). The map's rule claim that the children's preferential right operates only on intestacy was cited to section 24, whose text does not say that. Section 21(1) is the provision that confines Part III to inheritance ab intestato, so it is indispensable to the only part of the Q01 answer that disposes of the children's competing claim. Added as a supporting provision for Q01 and cited in CL-M010-Q01-003 and CL-M010-Q01-008.

2-1889/s545. The Q02 answer has Nihal transferring the house to Siripala, but nothing the researcher cited makes the grant of probate a condition of a transfer out of the estate. Section 545 forbids any transfer of property of a person dying testate within five years of the death unless probate has issued. Added as a supporting provision for Q02 and cited in CL-M010-Q02-014.

2-1889/s532(1). Two claims asserted that objections filed under the section 529 notice send the application to a final hearing on framed issues, citing only sections 529 and 534. Section 532(1) is the provision that does that, and the corpus edges show it procedurally requires section 524 on the same footing as section 531. Added as a supporting provision for Q02 and cited in CL-M010-Q02-006 and CL-M010-Q02-012.

question_decisions.note: statute_only confirmed: Wills Ordinance s.2(2) answers the question in express words and its closing clause displaces any contrary law, usage or custom, so no Roman-Dutch doctrine on the legitime is needed and none is cited. No case law appears anywhere in the answer. Indispensable set and the hop count of 2 confirmed; s.4 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance kept indispensable on the reading that 'execute' takes in the manner of execution, with the narrower reading recorded as a disagreement. One supporting provision added; every claim now rests on a provision that says what the claim says. The enrichment is the weak point and is flagged below rather than treated as a block, since added facts carry approval_status pending in any event.

statute_only confirmed: Chapter XXXVIII of the Civil Procedure Code sets out the sequence, the time limits and the forms as express duties. Every provision checked verbatim. Two supporting provisions added (ss.545 and 532) to ground the transfer step and the contested route. Hop count raised from 4 to 5 to match the six indispensable provisions in the chain. The rejection of ss.520, 523, 525 and 527 was checked and is right: ss.525 and 527 are worded for a person dying without a will, and s.520 requires security of an administrator appointed under s.518, not of an executor taking probate.

disagreements.researcher_position: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.4 is indispensable to Q01, because freedom of testation is exercisable only through a formally valid will.
disagreements.verifier_position: Kept indispensable, but the point is genuinely arguable. Q01 asks whether Martin can execute the will 'without assigning any reason'; read narrowly as a question only about giving reasons, s.4 drops to supporting and Q01 becomes a one-hop question on Wills Ordinance s.2(2) alone. The choice changes the hop count and the shape of the gold answer, so a lawyer should settle it.

disagreements.researcher_position: FACT-M010-Q01-006 states that Martin proposes to sign and place his thumb impression at the end of the will before a notary public and two witnesses present at the same time, and that neither witness benefits under the will or is married to anyone who does.
disagreements.verifier_position: This fact restates the tests in Prevention of Frauds Ordinance ss.4(2) and 11 almost word for word, so it hands the answering model the formality half of the answer without naming a statute. It is decisive in the sense the schema requires, but it removes the work from issue ISS-M010-Q01-03. A lawyer should decide between narrowing the fact to something neutral (for example, that the will was signed at a notary's office in the presence of two neighbours) and accepting the leak.

Five. The indispensable set is six provisions in a chain (ss.516, 517, 524, 531, 539, 551), which is five edges; the researcher's basis treated the oath and inventory under s.539 and the final account under s.551 as one step, but the twelve months for the account run from the issue of probate, which s.539 is a separate condition of. Changed in the map with the reason recorded.

temporal_issues: None found. The two 2022 amendments the map turns on were checked against the amending Acts themselves in the corpus: 29-2022/s2 repeals and substitutes Wills Ordinance s.2, and 30-2022/s3 inserts the thumb-impression and notary-plus-two-witnesses wording into Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.4. Both precede the 2026-04 reference date and the 20 August 2024 execution date in the Q02 enrichment.

Checked whether a later amendment was missed: Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024 is in the corpus but amends only section 2 of the principal enactment, not section 4, so the map's temporal note on PROV-M010-003 is complete. Wills (Amendment) No. 5 of 1993 amends only the since-repealed section 3.

The petition deadline of 17 May 2026 in the Q02 answer falls after the 2026-04 reference date. That is right for prospective advice, but it means the gold answer states a step that has not yet fallen due at the stated reference date.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: 15-1876/s21(1), the ab intestato limitation on Part III. Added as PROV-M010-901.
2-1889/s545, the bar on transferring estate property without a grant. Added as PROV-M010-902.
2-1889/s532(1), the route from objections to a final hearing. Added as PROV-M010-903. 2-1889/s533, which frames the issues, was checked and left out as duplicative of s.532 for this purpose.

Notaries Ordinance No. 1 of 1907 s.31, which the researcher flagged as a corpus gap, does contain will-specific duties: paragraph (h) requires the notary to set out in the attestation that the testator was in good and sound mind and to enter the will's number, date and testator's name in the deed register, and the requirement to read over and explain a deed in the presence of the attesting witnesses is expressly disapplied for wills. These bear on issue ISS-M010-Q01-03. Not added, because they are duties of the notary rather than conditions of the testator's power and so are supporting at best; a lawyer should decide whether Q01's gold answer should mention them.

Wills Ordinance s.7(2), as amended in 2022, directs testamentary proceedings on a joint will to Chapter XXXVIII or Chapter XXXVIIIB of the Civil Procedure Code. Chapter XXXVIIIB is not in the corpus (the section series jumps from s.554A to the insolvent-estates sections at s.554F). It does not affect this matter, which is not a joint will, but it is a corpus gap the map does not record.
case_law_dependence: None. Neither gold answer cites a case, and no claim depends on one. The Roman-Dutch doctrine of the legitime is displaced on the face of Wills Ordinance s.2(2), which is why Q01 survives as statute_only; if a lawyer takes the view that the abolition of the legitime still has to be shown from the common law, Q01 would have to be reserved.
enrichment_issues: FACT-M010-Q01-006 restates Prevention of Frauds Ordinance ss.4(2) and 11 almost verbatim as fact, which pre-answers the formality issue. Recorded as a disagreement.

FACT-M010-Q02-002 has the same shape on a smaller scale ('signing it and placing his thumb impression at the end before a notary public and two witnesses who were present together'), but Q02 does not turn on the manner of execution, so the leak is harmless there.

No statute name, section number or conclusion appears in either enriched background. Every synthetic_decisive fact carries a reason and a counterfactual, and all added facts are approval_status pending.

The enriched backgrounds put the estate at about Rs. 29.2 million against liabilities of about Rs. 350,000 plus funeral expenses. That is comfortably solvent, so the insolvent-estate sections (2-1889/s554F onwards) are correctly not engaged; a lawyer may wish to confirm the figures are meant to be that far apart.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: The two enriched backgrounds share the property description and the family facts, which is expected for a shared-background matter and is not a leak between questions.

Q01's enriched background is written prospectively ('proposes to sign') while Q02's has the will already executed on 20 August 2024. The two are consistent as successive stages of the same matter, but a scorer running them as independent items should be aware that Q01 is advice before execution and Q02 advice after death.

lawyer_questions: Q01, most important: is Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.4 part of the answer at all? If 'can he execute the will without assigning any reason' is read as a question only about giving reasons, Q01 collapses to one hop on Wills Ordinance s.2(2), PROV-M010-003 and PROV-M010-004 drop to background, and FACT-M010-Q01-006 (which restates the s.4 and s.11 tests almost verbatim and so leaks the formality answer) should be cut back or removed.

Q01: does the exclusion of the children need anything beyond the express words of Wills Ordinance s.2(2)? The corpus holds no provision on the legitime and no Roman-Dutch material; if the abolition of the legitime still has to be established from the common law, Q01 must be reserved rather than proposed_gold.

Q01: should Notaries Ordinance s.31(h) (the notary's duty to set out in the attestation that the testator was of good and sound mind, and to register the will) appear in the gold answer on the formalities issue?

Q02: is the answer right to have Nihal produce the will under s.516 and then petition under ss.517 and 524, or is production by a finder who is himself the named executor satisfied by the petition itself? The two steps are separately worded in the Code but overlap heavily on these facts.

Q02: does the twelve-month period in s.551 run from the issue of probate under s.539 or from the s.531 order? The answer assumes the issue of probate, which is also the basis for raising the hop count to 5.
Both questions: the claims carry supporting_fact_ids 'BG-1' and 'BG-2', which are not defined in the map. Confirm what they were meant to point at before this matter is scored.
